title: Release 1.9 gate fixes: skill frontmatter and CRLF-safe checks on Windows

known_failing.reason: two Go-dependent fixtures (go-vet-integration, worktree path) need a runnable go; this host blocks go.exe by Application Control; fails here at main 60d726d

tasks.objective: `claude plugin validate --strict .` fails on YAML frontmatter: the `description` of skills/pin-bump/SKILL.md, skills/unity-client-tech/SKILL.md and commands/assetgen.md contains an unquoted colon, so the frontmatter does not parse (the skills are not loaded as written). Fix each description so the frontmatter parses (quote it as a YAML string, or reword without the colon) with no change to its meaning, keep every other frontmatter key as is, then run `claude plugin validate --strict .` and `claude plugin validate --strict .claude-plugin/plugin.json` and report their exit codes. Changelog fragment changelog.d/frontmatter-yaml.md (### Fixed). Do not touch any other skill.
acceptance: both claude plugin validate --strict commands exit 0
the three descriptions keep their meaning and every other frontmatter key

tasks.objective: Four suites fail on a Windows host with git core.autocrlf=true although the code is right; make them line-ending safe. (1) scripts/checks/wire-parity.sh compares the two Wire.cs working-tree files with `cmp`; with autocrlf the server checkout is CRLF and the Netcode checkout LF, so identical committed files report 'differs' (the committed blobs of rpg-mmo-server 633a792 and Netcode 406a1b6 are byte-identical, sha256 5d67a41f81db). Compare with carriage returns removed from both sides (keep comparing the working tree: tests/checks-candidate.test.sh relies on an uncommitted worktree edit failing), print the sha256 of the CR-stripped content in the FAIL line, and say in the header comment that line endings are ignored. Add a test case to tests/checks-candidate.test.sh: same content with CRLF on one side passes, different content still fails. This also fixes the 'server env target is used' case. (2) tests/registry-fragments.test.sh 'split round trip' compares registry.json and the fragments byte for byte against a CRLF working tree: compare with CR removed (diff --strip-trailing-cr, cmp on tr -d CR), keep the check strict otherwise. (3) tests/art2d-workflow.test.sh runs `python3` in a subprocess, which on Windows is the Microsoft Store stub: use sys.executable (and any other bare `python3` subprocess in that test). Changelog fragment changelog.d/crlf-hosts.md (### Fixed). Run no suite beyond a syntax check; one verify session runs the tier command.
acceptance: wire-parity passes for identical content with CRLF on one side and fails for different content (test)
checks-candidate, registry-fragments and art2d-workflow pass on a host with autocrlf=true
no bare python3 subprocess in art2d-workflow.test.sh
